speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the lesions raised and do they have a central indentation or umbilication? Have you noticed any lesions on the child's face, scalp, or extremities?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of umbilicated, pearly papules in an immunized child with exposure to similar lesions is highly suggestive of Molluscum contagiosum. I will request images to confirm the classic appearance before finalizing the diagnosis. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Previously healthy, up-to-date immunizations, no significant illnesses. Social history: Attends daycare three times per week.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of pearly, umbilicated papules in an immunized 2-year-old with daycare exposure is classic for Molluscum contagiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
